tagline: Old turnpikes and a Quaker mill village in western Loudoun.
intro: Western Loudoun keeps a handful of old roads. Charles Town Pike comes down from Keyes Gap into the narrow valley called Between the Hills, then follows the North Fork of Catoctin Creek through Hillsboro Gap, a water gap the town of Hillsboro fills so completely that the road cannot be widened. Lanes wander off through Waterford, Lovettsville and Taylorstown.

Farther south the Snickersville Turnpike runs from Aldie to Bluemont, once Snickersville, a road that took over part of the first recorded turnpike in operation in the country, open by the end of 1786.

moments.title: Keyes Gap
moments.text: Once Vestal's Gap, at 906 feet one of the lowest crossings of the Blue Ridge in Virginia, and part of Braddock's army came through it with George Washington.

moments.title: Waterford
moments.text: Called Janney's Mill after the Quaker who built mills on Catoctin Creek in the 1740s, the village lay just southeast of the population center of the United States in 1810.

moments.title: Hibbs Bridge
moments.text: The turnpike crosses Beaverdam Creek on a stone double-arch bridge of about 1829, which local opposition has kept from being bypassed.
